title: SK Hynix Breaks Ground on $4 Billion Indiana HBM Fab as the AI Memory Supercycle Runs Hot
summary: SK Hynix committed over $4 billion to its first US HBM production base in Indiana, opening in 2028, just as the AI memory supercycle pushes pricing and margins to records. Here is what it means for US-listed plays like Micron, Nvidia and Broadcom.
body_markdown:
-


Gotrade News - SK Hynix broke ground on August 27 on a more than $4 billion advanced packaging plant at Purdue Research Park in West Lafayette, Indiana, its first high-bandwidth memory production base on US soil. According to[SK hynix's official announcement](https://news.skhynix.com/en/groundbreaking-ceremony-in-indiana/) , the site will open its cleanroom by October 2028 and begin mass production of next-generation HBM in the second half of 2029.


The timing matters because the memory that feeds AI accelerators is in the middle of a demand supercycle, and the companies that supply it are printing record margins. For US-listed investors, the read-through runs straight to memory maker[Micron Technology (MU)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mu/) and to the AI chip buyers, led by[NVIDIA Corp. (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) , that cannot get enough of it.


## Key Takeaways


- SK Hynix committed over $4 billion to an Indiana HBM packaging fab, with mass production slated for the second half of 2029.
- SK Hynix held a 58% HBM market share in Q1 2026 and posted a 76% operating margin in its latest quarter.
- Its CEO said he sees a memory shortage persisting through the end of 2030, with no clear signs of a downturn.
- Micron is the accessible US-listed way to own the memory theme, while Nvidia and Broadcom anchor the demand side.


## Why a $4 Billion HBM Base Is Landing in Indiana


The Indiana fab will take advanced wafers made in South Korea and handle packaging and testing in the US, the most complex and value-added step in building HBM. As reported by[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/sk-hynix-holds-groundbreaking-ceremony-for-4-billion-indiana-ai-chip-packaging-facility-4879737) , the plant is expected to run next-generation HBM4E and reach volume production in the third quarter of 2029, supported by $458 million in CHIPS Act grants and up to $500 million in loans finalized in December 2024. SK Hynix projects roughly 7,000 direct and indirect jobs and signed a research memorandum with Purdue University on advanced packaging.


Chief Executive Kwak Noh-Jung framed the investment as a long-term bet on US demand, saying the company will "become the most trusted partner in the U.S., where top-tier customers, R&D capabilities, and partners align." He has separately said he expects the current memory shortage to persist through the end of 2030, with "no clear signs of a memory downturn."
